Metadata.title: Hissiyat | Analysis dashboard
Metadata.description: An analysis dashboard for online human experience and search interest.

Dashboard.title: Analysis dashboard
Dashboard.intro: Explore online human experience and search interest.
Dashboard.notice: The charts in this section illustrate the interface with fictional text and search-interest data.

human.source: Fictional text data · Inspired by the CareerNet pilot
human.title: Human experience analysis
human.description: Topics, emotions, needs and experiences in writing about education and careers.
human.method: In these fixed fictional aggregates, each label counts the documents that carry it. Each share uses the selected cohort’s document total. A document can carry several labels, so shares can add up to more than 100%.
human.limit: Emotion labels reflect explicit expressions by fictional authors. These examples provide no evidence about psychological states, population prevalence, model performance or independent human evaluation.

caveats.general: A general sample from the fictional source frame. Shares use this cohort’s document count.
caveats.uncertainty-enriched: A sample enriched using fictional uncertainty cues. Its shares describe this cohort only.

search.source: Fictional time series · Inspired by Google Trends
search.title: Search interest analysis
search.description: A weekly relative interest index for a fictional search query.
search.coverage: {observed, number} of {weeks, number} weeks have values
search.chartLabel: Weekly fictional search interest. The line breaks at missing or suppressed weeks.
search.method: The fixed fictional series uses a relative index on a 0–100 scale. Missing and suppressed weeks have no numeric value and remain gaps in the line.
search.limit: The index contains no actual Google Trends measurements, counts of people or absolute search volumes. It is independent of the text cohorts and cannot establish causation between the two views.

states.invalid: The demo response did not match the expected contract.
states.empty: There is no demo data to display.
states.noCategories: There are no categories in this group.

LocalAnalysis.title: Analyze texts
LocalAnalysis.intro: Explore topic groups in a small collection of English texts with TF-IDF + NMF or MiniLM + K-means.
LocalAnalysis.inputHelp: Enter {min, number}–{max, number} texts, one per line, up to {chars, number} characters each. The application does not store the texts. Use fictional or appropriately de-identified test texts.
LocalAnalysis.resultSummary: {count, number} texts, {k, number} requested topic groups.
LocalAnalysis.nmfHelp: NMF uses word patterns. The terms shown are recurring words with high weights in this topic.
LocalAnalysis.minilmHelp: K-means groups MiniLM text vectors. The terms shown are lexical descriptors computed afterward from the assigned texts.
LocalAnalysis.agreementValue: Adjusted Rand index (ARI): {ari} across {count, number} texts assigned by both methods.
LocalAnalysis.agreementUnavailable: There are too few shared assignments or populated groups to report ARI.
LocalAnalysis.agreementHelp: ARI compares how the same texts are grouped, accounting for chance agreement. Topic accuracy requires independent thematic evaluation.
LocalAnalysis.unassigned: {count, plural, one {# text could not be assigned.} other {# texts could not be assigned.}}
LocalAnalysis.iterationLimit: The model reached its iteration limit. Interpret this grouping with extra care.
LocalAnalysis.limits: Group numbers are arbitrary and sizes describe only the submitted texts. A keyword must be in the permitted vocabulary and recur in at least three distinct texts in its group. The topics require human interpretation.

signals.title: Expressed Emotion, Need and Experience Signals
signals.denominator: Based on all {count, number} submitted texts.
signals.interpretation: Exploratory English phrase rules count each text at most once per category. A text can count in several categories. An unmarked text may still contain an emotion, need or experience. These counts describe matched expressions and provide no validated predictions or clinical assessments.

errors.tooLarge: Keep each text to 500 characters and the total request under 64 KiB.
errors.invalidInput: The local service rejected the input. Check the text lines and group count.
errors.insufficientVariation: The texts contain too little distinct vocabulary for this group count. Try more varied texts or select two groups.
errors.busy: An analysis is already running. Try again in a moment.
errors.modelUnavailable: The verified local MiniLM model could not be loaded. Check the local model setup, or select TF-IDF + NMF.
errors.unavailable: Local analysis is unavailable. Check that the local API is running with analysis enabled.

TrendsResearch.title: Google Trends Research API
TrendsResearch.source: Google Trends Research API · Authorized local series
TrendsResearch.fictional: Fictional adapter test · No Google API data
TrendsResearch.withheld: No verified local series is available. The dashboard has made no Google query.
TrendsResearch.scale: Search interest in original API units
TrendsResearch.chartLabel: Search-interest time series with gaps for missing and suppressed values
TrendsResearch.limits: Search interest describes relative search activity. It provides no absolute search counts or direct measurement of emotion, population experience, or causation. A single query covers a narrow part of search behavior.
TrendsResearch.alignment: Comparisons with other sources require aligned geography, time periods, and definitions. This series is displayed separately from the CareerNet text results.

Research.title: Research Findings
Research.sample: The first case study used {questions, number} reviewed English questions about careers.
Research.comparison: TF-IDF + NMF and MiniLM + K-means compared
Research.scale: Bars show the positive ARI values observed here on a 0–1 scale.
Research.ari: The adjusted Rand index (ARI) compares how the same questions are grouped and accounts for agreement expected by chance. A value of 1 means identical groupings, and a value near 0 indicates chance-level agreement. Classification accuracy is outside the scope of this experiment.
Research.stability: Stability shows how similar the clusters were across {repetitions, number} subsampling repetitions, each using about {share} of the sample.
Research.observed: Both methods were more stable with two clusters (k = 2) in the main experiment. Thematic validity and method superiority require further evidence.
Research.review: A first reviewer assigned the labels. A second reviewer independently assessed {questions, number} purposefully selected questions. Agreement varied by category. This small overlap sample is insufficient to establish general inter-rater reliability.
Research.limits: This small, selected English-language career sample describes the pilot only. Population estimates, clinical anxiety detection and causal inference are outside its scope.
Research.attribution: Hissiyat selected a sample from the dataset and compared methods. The analysis and interpretations belong to the Hissiyat project. Attribution implies no publisher endorsement.
